probe: PROBE 2B - independent reproduction of the kill condition, and the salvage path for F2
why: PROBE 2 concluded KeeperHub refuses to broadcast a call it predicts will revert, which breaks the literal mechanism behind PRD F2. Before rewriting the PRD around that, the finding was reproduced independently, and the remaining question was answered: can a reverted transaction still be put on-chain at all?

partA_reproduction.claim: KeeperHub rejects a guaranteed-revert call pre-broadcast even with simulate:false
partA_reproduction.onChain: no executionId, no transactionHash, nothing broadcast

partB_salvage.question: If KeeperHub will not broadcast a doomed call, can anyone? A reverted transaction with a real hash is the whole point of F2.
partB_salvage.method: cast send with an explicit --gas-limit, which skips eth_estimateGas and therefore skips the client-side revert prediction that normally blocks the send

senderNonce.meaning: nonce advanced - the transaction really was broadcast, not simulated

partB_salvage.verdict: CONFIRMED. A reverted transaction CAN be placed on Base Sepolia with a real, permanent hash. The blocker is KeeperHub's pre-broadcast simulation, not the chain and not the contract.

consequenceForF2.whatDies: The claim that KeeperHub itself broadcasts the doomed call. It does not, and three independent execution paths confirm it (PROBE 2 trials A/B/C). Any wording that says 'the agent broadcast a transaction that reverted' is false as executed through KeeperHub.
consequenceForF2.whatSurvives: Everything the evidence is actually for. Restructured into three layers, each independently checkable:

layer1_agentRefusal.mechanism: check-and-execute with the guard condition on a healthy position evaluates conditionResult.met=false, executed=false
layer1_agentRefusal.proves: the agent looked, and stood down
layer1_agentRefusal.status: shape already validated by PROBE 3 (zero-arg condition + zero-arg action works end-to-end)

layer2_contractRefusal.source: Base Sepolia, via a direct call with an explicit gas limit
layer2_contractRefusal.mechanism: call guardRepay() on a healthy vault; the tx mines with status 0x0 and the Refused_* error in its revert data
layer2_contractRefusal.proves: the contract refuses regardless of who calls it - the guarantee does not depend on the agent behaving
layer2_contractRefusal.status: mechanism proven here on Probe.boom(); repeat on the real vault once deployDemoVault has run

layer3_exhaustiveness.proves: every Refused_* path has a test, so layer 2 is a sample of a proven set, not a lucky screenshot

consequenceForF2.narrativeNote: This is a stronger submission than the original, not a weaker one: the team probed the platform, found documented behaviour that contradicted their design assumption, published the negative result, and adapted. Present the KeeperHub refusal as the safety property it is - a platform that declines to burn gas on a call it knows will fail - and let the chain-side evidence come from a direct call. Do not paper over which party broadcast what.
